sources.entry: Lago - Metering and usage-based billing. (Source Code) AGPL-3.0 Docker

summary.one_liner: Lago is an open-source, API-first billing platform that meters product usage (including AI tokens and compute), applies pricing and credits, and generates invoices and payment collection.
summary.what_it_does: Ingests usage events from applications and turns them into billable metrics with support for many pricing models (usage-based, prepaid, graduated, volume, package, minimum commitment, hybrid). It handles subscriptions, prepaid credit wallets, entitlements, invoices, credit notes, taxes, and multiple currencies and entities. It orchestrates payments through providers such as Stripe, Adyen, and GoCardless, with retries and dunning. The README describes REST API, SDKs (Node.js, Python, Ruby, Go), webhooks, an MCP server, and a CLI for programmatic and agent-driven access. A local Docker Compose setup is documented for self-hosting, and a demo script prices sample AI token usage.
use_cases: meter API calls or AI token usage and bill customers
usage-based or prepaid billing for SaaS products
generate invoices and collect payments from usage
self-host a billing and subscription system
manage credits, allowances and entitlements for customers
automate billing workflows through an API or AI agent
how_to_run: Optional local AI pricing demo: ./examples/agentic-ai-demo/run.sh (requires Docker, curl, jq)
notable: Idempotent event ingestion keyed by transaction_id, so retries do not double-bill
Atomic batch ingestion: an invalid event causes the whole batch to be rejected
Headless, API-first design with an MCP server and CLI for AI agents
Supports both direct use (own product) and embedded white-label billing for platforms
Dedicated workers can be scaled separately for events, invoices, payments and webhooks
caveats: Some features (Billing Assistant, enterprise integrations, governance, embedded white-label use) are Premium or available on request
Managed Lago Cloud is a commercial offering; the README points to contacting sales for it
Self-hosting requires configuring database, Redis, SMTP, TLS and object storage for production, per the deployment guide
